newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian ice fishermen plucked to safety.
newsitem.headline: Russian ice fishermen plucked to safety.

text.p: Rescuers plucked four Russian fishing enthusiasts from drifting ice on Lake Ladoga on Friday after saving nearly 40 fishermen the day before.

Many others, glad to avoid the expense of a helicopter rescue, found their own way ashore after ice floes broke away with the spring thaw. But at least one of several cars was left precariously afloat on the inland sea near St. Petersburg.
An Emergencies Ministry spokesman in the city told Reuters that up to 100 fishermen with about six cars were reported missing on Thuesday as the ice broke up.

Many escaped when they drifted back to shore in the wind. It is not uncommon for the hardy ice anglers to refuse helicopter rescue -- for which there can be a hefty fee. They prefer to sit tight and hope for an onshore breeze.

Fishing through holes cut in the ice is popular with millions of Russians. Vodka keeps out the cold and dulls any fear of falling through or drifting away -- fates which claim many lives every winter, especially late in the cold season.
